headline: Metro Manila Cities Suspend Afternoon Classes as Habagat Rains Persist
seoTitle: Metro Manila Afternoon Classes Suspended on August 13
seoDescription: Several Metro Manila local governments suspended afternoon face-to-face classes on August 13 as southwest monsoon rains persisted.
deck: Several Metro Manila local governments suspended afternoon face-to-face classes on August 13 as southwest monsoon rains continued.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Several Metro Manila local governments suspended afternoon face-to-face classes on Thursday, August 13, as heavy rain associated with the southwest monsoon continued.

Quezon City suspended afternoon face-to-face classes in public Child Development Centers and public schools from kindergarten through Grade 12. Caloocan covered all levels in public and private schools; Mandaluyong covered preschool through Grade 12, including ALS; and Pasig covered kindergarten through Grade 12 in public and private schools. Makati, Parañaque, Pasay, San Juan, Manila and Las Piñas also announced afternoon suspensions with varying coverage.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Valenzuela, Malabon and Marikina were listed under broader no-face-to-face-class declarations rather than the narrower afternoon-only updates. Many affected schools shifted to alternative delivery modes, depending on the local advisory.

Suspension coverage differed by city, grade level and school type. Parents and students should check the original local-government or school announcement because conditions and instructions can change.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Precisely stating the covered hours, grade levels and school types helps families avoid unnecessary travel during heavy rain and prevents a citywide advisory from being misread as applying to schools or levels it does not cover.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Monitor official local-government, school and PAGASA channels for later changes, including any extension of suspensions, shifts to alternative learning, road flooding or updated rainfall warnings.
